methods.label: Find the excess over 1
methods.explanation:
Using the common denominator \(120\) turns the question into matching integer numerators. The original sum is
\[
\frac{60+30+20+15+12+10}{120}
=\frac{147}{120}.
\]
To leave \(1=120/120\), we must remove \(27/120\). The only pair of these numerators adding to \(27\) is \(15\) and \(12\): \(60\) and \(30\) are too large, \(20\) would require an absent \(7\), and among \(15,12,10\), only \(15+12\) works.

These numerators correspond to \(15/120=1/8\) and \(12/120=1/10\). Remove \(\frac18\) and \(\frac1{10}\), choice E.
